message: ## Summary This PR implements a comprehensive offline license validation system and attribution comments for React on Rails Pro. ### Key Features - **Offline JWT license validation** using RSA-256 signatures - **Production grace period** (1 month) for ANY expired license in production - **Attribution comments** in rendered HTML showing license status - **Dual validation**: Ruby gem (startup) + Node renderer (startup) - **No internet required**: Validation uses embedded public keys ## Motivation React on Rails Pro needs a licensing system that: - **Works offline**: No phone-home or internet dependency - **Provides flexibility**: FREE evaluation licenses for dev/test/CI (duration in JWT) - **Protects production**: Grace period prevents sudden outages when licenses expire - **Is transparent**: Attribution comments show what's running ## Implementation Details ### License Validation **API Design (Ruby & Node.js are aligned):** Both Ruby and Node.js implementations use the same API pattern: - **Primary method**: `getValidatedLicenseData()` / `validated_license_data!` - Validates license and returns data - Caches result for performance - Exits process if invalid - **Helper methods**: `isEvaluation()` / `evaluation?`, `getGraceDaysRemaining()` / `grace_days_remaining` - **Testing method**: `reset()` / `reset!` to clear cache **Ruby Implementation** (`react_on_rails_pro/lib/react_on_rails_pro/license_validator.rb`): ```ruby # Main API ReactOnRailsPro::LicenseValidator.validated_license_data! # Returns hash with license data ReactOnRailsPro::LicenseValidator.evaluation? # true if free/evaluation license ReactOnRailsPro::LicenseValidator.grace_days_remaining # Integer or nil ReactOnRailsPro::LicenseValidator.reset! # Clear cache (testing) ``` **Node.js Implementation** (`packages/node-renderer/src/shared/licenseValidator.ts`): ```typescript // Main API getValidatedLicenseData() // Returns LicenseData interface isEvaluation() // true if free/evaluation license getGraceDaysRemaining() // number | undefined reset() // Clear cache (testing) ``` **Grace Period Behavior:** The grace period applies **ONLY in production environments** and is **1 month for ALL licenses** (free and paid): - **Production Environment** (`NODE_ENV=production` / `Rails.env.production?`): - ✅ **Grace period**: 1 month (30 days) after license expires - ⚠️ **During grace**: Logs ERROR messages on every startup showing days remaining - ✅ **Continues running**: Application stays operational during grace period - ❌ **After grace**: Application fails to start - **Non-Production Environments** (development, test, CI): - ❌ **No grace period**: Application exits immediately when license expires - 🎯 **Purpose**: Helps catch expiration issues early in development/testing **Why this design?** - Production deployments need buffer time to renew licenses without downtime - Development/test environments should fail fast to catch expiration before production - Same grace period for all license types keeps behavior predictable **License Sources** (checked in order): 1. Environment variable: `REACT_ON_RAILS_PRO_LICENSE` 2. Config file: `config/react_on_rails_pro_license.key` **JWT Structure:** ```json { "sub": "user@example.com", // Email (REQUIRED) "iat": 1234567890, // Issued at timestamp (REQUIRED) "exp": 1234567890, // Expiration timestamp (REQUIRED) - duration set by issuer "plan": "free", // "free" or "paid" or "paid_*" (Optional) "organization": "Your Company", // Company name (Optional) "iss": "api" // Issuer (Optional) } ``` **License Duration:** - License duration is **encoded in the JWT's `exp` (expiration) field** - **Free evaluation**: Typically 3 months (set when JWT is issued) - **Paid licenses**: Duration based on subscription (e.g., 1 year, 2 years) - set when JWT is issued - The validation code doesn't hardcode durations - it only checks if `exp` < current time ### Attribution Comments **HTML Comments in Rendered Output:** - Added to all Rails views using React on Rails - Shows version info and license status - Example output: ```html ``` **Implementation:** - `ReactOnRailsPro::Utils.pro_attribution_comment` generates comment - Integrated into view helpers automatically - Shows grace period warnings when applicable ### Testing **Ruby Tests** (`react_on_rails_pro/spec/react_on_rails_pro/license_validator_spec.rb`): - ✅ Valid license validation - ✅ Expired license handling (production grace period vs non-production immediate exit) - ✅ Missing required fields - ✅ Invalid signature detection - ✅ Missing license error - ✅ Caching behavior - ✅ Environment vs file loading - ✅ `evaluation?` method for different plans - ✅ `reset!` functionality **Node.js Tests** (`packages/node-renderer/tests/licenseValidator.test.ts`): - ✅ Valid license from environment variable - ✅ Expired license in non-production (exits immediately) - ✅ Missing expiration field - ✅ Invalid signature - ✅ Missing license - ✅ Caching validation results - ✅ `isEvaluation()` for free vs paid licenses - ✅ `reset()` clears cache ## Changes by Component ### Ruby Gem (`react_on_rails_pro/`) **New Files:** - `lib/react_on_rails_pro/license_validator.rb` - Main validation logic - `lib/react_on_rails_pro/license_public_key.rb` - RSA public key - `spec/react_on_rails_pro/license_validator_spec.rb` - Comprehensive tests **Modified Files:** - `lib/react_on_rails_pro/utils.rb` - Added `pro_attribution_comment` method - `react_on_rails_pro.gemspec` - Added `jwt` gem dependency (~> 2.7) - `.gitignore` - Added `config/react_on_rails_pro_license.key` ### Node Renderer (`react_on_rails_pro/packages/node-renderer/`) **New Files:** - `src/shared/licenseValidator.ts` - Validation module (functional pattern) - `src/shared/licensePublicKey.ts` - Public key for Node - `tests/licenseValidator.test.ts` - Jest tests **Modified Files:** - `src/master.ts` - Added license validation on startup - `package.json` - Added `jsonwebtoken` dependency (^9.0.0) ### Documentation **New Files:** - `react_on_rails_pro/LICENSE_SETUP.md` - Complete license setup guide - Getting FREE evaluation licenses - Installation methods (ENV var vs config file) - Grace period explanation - Troubleshooting guide - FAQ section - `react_on_rails_pro/CI_SETUP.md` - CI/CD configuration guide - Step-by-step for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Travis, Jenkins, Bitbucket - License renewal process - Security best practices **Modified Files:** - `CHANGELOG.md` - Added attribution comment feature - `react_on_rails_pro/CHANGELOG.md` - Added license validation system and attribution comment ## How It Works ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 1. License Storage │ │ ├─ ENV['REACT_ON_RAILS_PRO_LICENSE'] │ │ └─ config/react_on_rails_pro_license.key │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 2. Validation Points │ │ ├─ Ruby Gem: Rails startup │ │ │ └─ ReactOnRailsPro::LicenseValidator.validated_license_data! │ │ └─ Node Renderer: Node startup │ │ └─ getValidatedLicenseData() │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 3. Validation Logic │ │ ├─ JWT.verify(token, PUBLIC_KEY, algorithm: 'RS256') │ │ ├─ Check required fields (sub, iat, exp) │ │ ├─ Check expiration: │ │ │ ├─ PRODUCTION: 1-month grace period for any license │ │ │ └─ NON-PROD: Fail immediately │ │ └─ Cache result for performance │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 4. Outcomes │ │ ├─ Valid: App starts, cache license data │ │ ├─ Expired in Production: │ │ │ ├─ Within grace period (30 days): Continue + ERROR logs │ │ │ └─ After grace period: Exit │ │ └─ Expired in Dev/Test/CI: Exit immediately │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 5. Attribution │ │ └─ HTML comment added to rendered views │ │ "React on Rails Pro: [license status]" │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ## License Types ### FREE Evaluation License - **Duration**: Set in JWT `exp` field (typically 3 months from issue date) - **Usage**: Personal, educational, evaluation purposes (dev/test/CI) - **NOT for production deployment** - **Get it**: https://shakacode.com/react-on-rails-pro - **Expiration behavior**: - Development/Test/CI: Fails immediately on expiration - Production: 1-month grace period, then fails - **Renewal**: Get new FREE license every time it expires ### Paid License - **Duration**: Set in JWT `exp` field based on subscription (e.g., 1 year, 2 years) - **Usage**: Production deployment - **Includes**: Professional support - **Expiration behavior**: - Development/Test/CI: Fails immediately on expiration - Production: 1-month grace period, then fails - **Renewal**: Contact ShakaCode before expiration **Note**: Grace period behavior is the same for both license types - only the initial duration (encoded in `exp`) differs. ## Security Features - ✅ **Offline validation**: No internet or phone-home required - ✅ **RSA-256 signatures**: Cannot be forged without private key - ✅ **Tamper-proof**: Any modification invalidates signature - ✅ **Algorithm enforcement**: Only RS256 accepted (prevents downgrade attacks) - ✅ **No tracking**: License validated locally using cryptography - ✅ **Config file in .gitignore**: Prevents accidental commits ## Breaking Changes None. This is a new feature for React on Rails Pro. ## Migration Guide For existing React on Rails Pro users: 1. **Get a license** (FREE evaluation): https://shakacode.com/react-on-rails-pro 2. **Set environment variable** or create config file 3. **That's it!** - Your app will validate on startup See `react_on_rails_pro/LICENSE_SETUP.md` for detailed instructions. ## Test Plan - [x] Ruby specs pass (15 examples, 0 failures) - [x] Node tests pass (9 examples, 0 failures) - [x] ESLint passes with 0 errors - [x] RuboCop passes with 0 offenses - [x] All git hooks pass - [x] License file properly ignored in git - [x] Attribution comments appear in rendered HTML - [x] Grace period logic tested (production vs non-production) - LICENSE_SETUP.md and CI_SETUP.md written 3. ⏳ **Replace placeholder keys** - Use ShakaCode's actual RSA key pair 4. ⏳ **Set up license generation** - Backend service for issuing licenses 5. ⏳ **End-to-end testing** - Test with real licenses in example apps 6. ⏳ **Deploy to users** - Release with next version ## FAQ **Q: Why do I need a license for development?** A: FREE evaluation licenses let us track usage and provide better support. Registration takes 30 seconds! **Q: What happens when my license expires in development?** A: The app fails to start immediately (no grace period in dev/test/CI). This helps you catch expiration early before it affects production. **Q: What happens when my license expires in production?** A: You get a 1-month grace period with ERROR logs showing days remaining. This gives you time to renew without downtime. Monitor your logs! **Q: Is the grace period different for free vs paid licenses?** A: No! Both get the same 1-month grace period in production. The difference is the initial license duration (encoded in the JWT's `exp` field). **Q: Can I use free licenses in production?** A: Free licenses are intended for evaluation only (dev/test/CI). Production should use paid licenses, but technically both work the same way with the same grace period. **Q: Does validation require internet?** A: No! Everything is validated offline using cryptographic signatures. **Q: How long do licenses last?** A: License duration is set when the JWT is issued: - Free evaluation: Typically 3 months - Paid: Based on your subscription (e.g., 1 year, 2 years) --- 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) Co-Authored-By: Claude - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/shakacode/react_on_rails/1857)
